It said simply: “The bridge is fucked.” He then added: “We will stand and Moscow will fall.” It was a freezing night, with a bright starry sky and no clouds. Lines of ice had formed on the drone’s bulky wings. Soon, it would be hurtling towards its target – about 500km to the south.

Typically the soldiers who gathered in this muddy field in central Ukraine were attacking oil refineries deep inside Russia. In recent months the work had become almost mundane: they had hit so many of them. The objective that evening, however, was unique. It was a structure personally associated with Vladimir Putin and his grandiose imperial ambitions.

Knesset’s appointment of Matan Kahana marks step towards reversing policies of outgoing government

The Israeli parliament elected a new speaker on Tuesday, a key step toward rolling back policies passed by the outgoing government led by the prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu.

The new speaker is Matan Kahana, an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, the party leader currently working to form the next government and replace Netanyahu.

events.title: Palestinian woman shot dead by Israeli settlers near Jericho, witnesses say
events.summary:
Bullet hit 72-year-old Fadha Wadha in head outside her home in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, in the West Bank, say residents

A 72-year-old Palestinian woman has been shot dead in an overnight attack by Israeli settlers in a village near Jericho where settlers have recently moved in after taking over several Palestinian homes.

Fadha Wadha was standing outside her home in al-Duyuk al-Tahta in the occupied West Bank when she was struck in the head by a bullet as Israeli settlers fired towards Palestinian houses, according to testimonies from residents. Several other Palestinians, including her son, were wounded by gunfire.

events.title: Anti-Arab hate speech surged on social media during Israel’s election, report finds
events.summary:
Digital monitors recorded 400% rise in posts attacking Arab Israelis, including Netanyahu’s disproven fraud allegations

Anti-Arab hate speech surged on social media in Israel around the country’s general election last month, digital monitors have said, as politicians including Benjamin Netanyahu levelled disproven allegations against Arab Israeli parties of election fraud.

A new report by the Israel-based Brandeis Institute and FakeReporter recorded a deluge of anti-Arab discourse across social media platforms such as X, Facebook, Instagram and TikTok in the days surrounding Israel’s 27 October election.

Trump said his administration takes the idea “very seriously”

events.title: India has been named a ‘destination of the year’ for 2027 – here are insiders’ tips on travelling beyond the tropes
events.summary:
As tourism booms, three experienced female travellers give their take on how to make the most of travelling here

• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

The 13th-century Persian scholar Zakariyya al-Qazwini never travelled to India. But he catalogued it in his famous work The Wonders of Creation and Rarities of Existence, which drew on accounts of a distant land filled with “rarities par excellence”. For al-Qazwini, as Helen Pfeifer writes in the London Review of Books, wonder was not an emotion but an intellectual method of making sense of the world and acquiring knowledge.

India has long occupied such a space in the global imagination, as a land of extraordinary riches; spirituality, customs, chaos and contradictions. This has shaped how the country is perceived from afar, but it can often flatten its complexities.

When the floods hit Pakistan he went out to help. Then the water reached his own family. This is Imran Lodhi’s story

Location: Dera Ghazi Khan, Pakistan

Disaster: Pakistan intense monsoon rainfall

Imran Lodhi is a university lecturer with a doctorate in climate change and sustainable development. The 41-year-old was living in Dera Ghazi Khan, a city in south-western Punjab, when floods devastated provinces across Pakistan. Climate change made the monsoon rainfall that caused the floods more intense.

events.title: World’s top court to rule if Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya
events.summary:
International court of justice has never before found a state guilty of genocide, and ruling will have implications for case against Israel

The world’s top court will deliver a judgment this week on whether Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, in a landmark case that will set a critical 21st-century benchmark for the gravest of all international crimes.

The closely watched judgment could become one of the most significant moments in international law since the end of the second world war.

events.title: Disgraced former leader Sheikh Hasina plans return to Bangladesh from exile
events.summary:
Former prime minister faces death penalty upon return after being sentenced in absentia over deaths in 2024 uprising

Sheikh Hasina is “confident” she will return to Bangladesh in December, according to exiled members of her party, after the disgraced former prime minister applied for a new passport this week.

Hasina has been living in self-imposed exile since August 2024 when she was toppled from power by a mass uprising against her authoritarian rule. She crossed the border to India, where she has since been allowed to live freely in Delhi.

events.title: Grenades, grief and a deepening political divide: five takeaways from Sonia Gandhi’s new memoir
events.summary:
From the assassinations of her husband and mother-in-law to press stonewalling under Modi, Belonging offers an insider’s account of India’s political evolution

• Don’t get This is India delivered to your inbox? Sign up here

Few love stories have been as closely entwined with a nation’s history as that of Sonia and Rajiv Gandhi. The former’s much-awaited political memoir, Belonging, offers a strikingly candid account of her journey from a small town in Italy to the highest echelons of power in India – all for love, she says.

The veteran Congress party leader has been fiercely protective of her personal world. In Belonging, she opens up for the first time about the extraordinary twists and turns of a life that has largely unfolded in full public view. (The Guardian’s Hannah Ellis-Petersen has a rare in-person interview with Gandhi, and you can read an excerpt from the book here.)

events.summary:
Lt Col Brandon Carroll Tyner was arrested by British police on 10 November over allegations related to espionage

A US soldier who was arrested in the UK on suspicion of spying for Russia has been taken into custody by the US military, police have said.

Lt Col Brandon Carroll Tyner, 41, was detained by British counter-terrorism police ‌on 10 November in Gloucestershire over allegations relating ⁠to espionage.

events.title: UK will miss climate targets if it weakens EV sales rules, advisers warn
events.summary:
Analysts say mooted move to let more petrol and diesel vehicles be sold would wreck plan to reach net zero by 2050

Weakening the UK’s electric car sales rules would probably cause the government to miss legally binding climate targets, according to advisers tracking Britain’s progress to net zero.

The analysis by the Climate Change Committee (CCC) suggests the policy would blow a hole in the plan for achieving net zero carbon emissions by 2050 – prompting concerns that Andy Burnham’s government will have to slash the UK’s carbon emissions reduction targets, known as the carbon budgets.

events.title: Shabana Mahmood to launch fast-track training to improve police leadership
events.summary:
After damning report into standards at the top of forces in England and Wales, 200 people a year with superintendent potential to be recruited

Shabana Mahmood will tell police chiefs and leaders at their central London annual conference on Wednesday that standards must improve as she unveils a scheme to train 200 people a year, after a report in June into police leadership found it was at times “staggeringly” poor.

events.title: Ofqual urges ‘life-altering’ penalties for students who use tech to cheat
events.summary:
England’s exam regulator says those caught using AI or smart glasses face disqualification from GCSEs and A-levels

Students in England could suffer “life-altering” penalties if they are caught relying on AI or smart glasses to cheat, England’s qualifications regulator has said.

The head of Ofqual, Ian Bauckham, said students could be disqualified from GCSEs, A-levels and other qualifications if they tried to use AI in assessed coursework, and called for retailers to be barred from marketing wearable technology for exam cheating.

events.title: Hundreds protest against Nathan Cofnas talk on DEI at Oriel College in Oxford

Students oppose appearance of self-described ‘race realist’ who made plagiarism claims against Jason Arday

Hundreds of protesters filled the cobbled streets around Oriel College, Oxford, to voice their opposition to an appearance by Nathan Cofnas, the self-described “race realist”.

The event organised by the university’s Reform UK student society – billed as “An evening with Nathan Cofnas: is DEI undermining higher education?” – went ahead on Tuesday evening despite opposition from students, college staff and local politicians concerned that his appearance would create a hostile environment.

A pair of waterspouts were recorded recently in the San Francisco Bay area, much to the delight and shock of several observers, as storms pummelled the region.

Two waterspouts – vortexes of air and water mist, essentially tornadoes – cut a sheer streak into the sky, as they spiraled above the bay, according to social media footage capturing the weather phenomenon.

events.title: White House withdraws nomination of Heidi Overton to lead FDA
events.summary:
Move to drop Trump ally and prominent abortion opponent comes a day before key Senate health committee vote

The White House has dropped its nomination of Heidi Overton to lead the Food and Drug Administration, a White House official told the Guardian.

Donald Trump nominated Overton – a physician and prominent abortion opponent – in August. Overton has spent most of her professional career working directly for Trump or conservative groups aligned with his agenda. Her nomination in August was seen as a move to bring a stabilizing Trump loyalist to the agency after a tumultous year under Trump’s first FDA commissioner, Marty Makary.

events.title: Man armed with axe accused of destroying US military plane at Shannon airport in Ireland
events.summary:
Daithi O’Corrain charged with destruction of US government property, after allegedly smashing gauges and cutting hydraulic lines

An axe-wielding man breached a security perimeter and destroyed an American military plane while it was parked at an Irish airport, US prosecutors said.

Daithi O’Corrain, 48, is accused of cutting hydraulic lines, smashing cockpit gauges and pouring ball bearings into fuel tanks.

events.title: Nvidia doubles revenue as board says it does not intend to reinstate Jensen Huang
events.summary:
Company issues first earnings report after ouster of CEO over allegations of affair with suspected Chinese spy

Nvidia “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO”, the chairman of the company’s board said Tuesday. Harvey Jones made the remark during Nvidia’s first quarterly earnings report since Jensen Huang’s ouster.

Nvidia announced the same day that its quarterly revenue beat expectations, coming in at $115.84bn, doubling from the same time period a year ago. The third-quarter earnings report comes just days after the world’s most valuable chip company saw the ouster of Huang over allegations of several extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy and two with his own employees.

events.title: British counterterrorism police arrest US soldier accused of spying on behalf of Russia

events.title: UK Privy Council overrules Trinidad and Tobago gay sex law

events.title: Bulgaria highway pileup kills 12, dozens injured: PM

events.title: Borussia Dortmund's Felix Nmecha and the question of religion

events.summary: The European Union wants to relax rules for pesticides, saying it will be easier for farmers to adopt more environmentally friendly options. But health and environmental experts say the risks are far too great.

events.summary: As US sanctions expand to Iran's rail sector, Tehran is relying more heavily on overland links with China and Central Asia. But capacity constraints, delays and costs limit rail's ability to replace maritime trade.

events.title: Rising emissions and temperatures: The cost of Trump's climate retreat is now clear

events.summary: Nvidia's board chairman ruled out bringing back co-founder Jensen Huang as CEO on Tuesday, as the chipmaker forecast stronger-than-expected quarterly sales but faced growing questions over its leadership, national security exposure and long-term strategy following his abrupt departure.

events.title: WHO sounds the alarm on antimicrobial resistance threat
events.summary: The spread of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is threatening modern medicine despite progress in combating drug-resistant bacteria, senior World Health Organization officials said Monday. WHO officials said countries had expanded efforts to tackle AMR, but warned that progress in prevention, diagnosis and the appropriate use of antibiotics remained too slow to meet global targets. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Jean Pierre Nyemazi, Acting Director of the WHO's AMR Department.

events.title: US, Mexico and Bolivia lose measles-free status as deaths mount
events.summary: The US has lost its measles-free status, international health officials said Tuesday, as the highly contagious virus has spread at the fastest rate in more than 30 years, while Mexico and Bolivia also lost their measles-elimination status. Vaccination rates have been falling against a number of diseases, in the US and globally, and measles has been spreading throughout the Americas since 2024.

events.title: 🔴Israeli parliament elects Eisenkot ally Matan Kahana as new Knesset speaker
Israeli parliament elects Eisenkot ally Matan Kahana as speaker in blow for Netanyahu
events.summary: The Israeli parliament on Tuesday elected as new speaker an ally of Gadi Eisenkot, the party leader currently working to form the next government and replace current Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Matan Kahana, a former special forces soldier, is expected as soon as Wednesday to start the process of undoing much of the agenda of Netanyahu.

events.title: AI imagery complicates Nigeria's election prep
events.summary: In tonight's edition, concerns emerge that AI has been used to generate fake voting profiles ahead of Nigeria's high-stakes general election in January. Also, Nigeria's mining marshal heads underground to unearth some of the people and organizations behind the vast illegal mining industries. And a groundbreaking archaeological discovery in northern Sudan could be the ancient site of the largest church ever built in one of medieval Nubia's most important Christian sites.

events.title: Major setbacks for Netanyahu ahead of vote to name new Knesset speaker
events.summary: Since suffering heavy losses in Israel’s Oct. 27 election, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's party has repeatedly claimed the vote was “stolen” by Arab-led parties, possibly with foreign assistance. Those claims appear to be crumbling as he tries to cling to power, as the Israeli parliament is set to select a new speaker opposed to him. FRANCE 24's Noga Tarnopolsky reports from Jerusalem.

events.title: Jensen Huang says he'd be honoured to return to Nvidia as CEO
events.summary: Jensen Huang makes his first public statement since resigning from Nvidia, saying he'd be honoured to return to his job amid support from the tech world. It comes ahead of a much anticipated earnings call this Tuesday, with analysts expecting the group to report a 90% jump in revenue to about $109 billion.

events.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang: Targeted by the AI misinformation he helped create
events.summary: Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang has become the target of a wave of AI-generated misinformation, in a striking twist for one of the men behind the AI revolution. From a fake audio recording supposedly featuring his wife to fabricated LinkedIn profiles, false claims linking him to the Chinese Communist Party and viral AI memes, Vedika Bahl examines how deepfakes and misinformation are turning against the former tech boss in Truth or Fake.

events.title: Iran 'playing mind games with the United States', expert says
events.summary: President Donald Trump said Tuesday that US authorities take "very seriously" any possible threat to Washington, following reports Iran was planning to target officials, possibly with a radioactive bomb. Speaking with FRANCE 24's Monte Francis, Barbara Slavin, Distinguished Fellow at the Stimson Center in Washington, says that Iran may be "playing mind games with the United States as a way perhaps of deterring President Trump from unleashing a massive new attack on Iran".

events.title: Authorities take over Turkey's last pro-opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV
events.summary: Police raided the Istanbul headquarters of Sozcu TV on Tuesday, dealing another significant blow to Turkey's pro-opposition media. This is the third such seizure of pro-opposition media in just over a year. It comes amid public uproar over a multi-billion investment fund scandal that has affected the savings of nearly half a million people and piled pressure on President Recep Tayyip Erdogan's ruling AKP party ahead of elections in 2028. FRANCE 24's Jasper Mortimer reports from Ankara.

events.title: The centre cannot hold? Splintered moderates lag in French presidential race
events.summary: Five months to go before the French vote in the presidential election first round to choose Emmanuel Macron’s successor. Not much of a race so far for the top two spots and the May Second runoff: there’s the far-right’s Marine Le Pen, the far-left’s Jean-Luc Mélenchon and way behind there’s the rest. Whether on social media or in the streets, their supporters rule. A radical break with the mainstream.

events.title: France: Protesters march for better salaries across the country
events.summary: Tens of thousands of people took part in protests across France on Tuesday after unions called a new nationwide public sector strike to demand pay rises. What started over two months ago as high school student protests has now morphed into a wider movement against the increasing cost of living.

events.title: 'A lot of anger and a weak government': Why are French public sector workers striking?

events.title: Deutsche Bank leaks: German lender's dealings with Russian oligarchs under scrutiny

events.title: Latest cost-of-living protests bring more than 140,000 onto the streets across France
events.summary: Tens of thousands of people took part in protests across France on Tuesday after unions called a new nationwide public sector strike to demand pay rises. Participation was lower compared to previous demonstrations, with 146,000 people demonstrating across the country, according to the interior ministry, compared with 575,000 for the previous unified protests. Unions put Tuesday's number at 550,000.

events.title: Organisers hoping for 'joyful' demonstration as French public workers strike
events.summary: France braced for another day of protests Tuesday as unions called for a nationwide strike by public sector workers in a bid to secure pay rises. Hoping to avoid the violence that has marred recent protests in the country, organisers were hoping for a "joyous and festive" occasion, reports France 24's Claire Paccalin from a march in Paris.

events.title: Shenzhen: Inside ‘China’s Silicon Valley’

events.summary: A widespread outage continued to hit Microsoft platforms including Outlook on Friday, with many users encountering trouble using their email accounts.

events.title: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills at least six people, officials say
events.summary: An Israeli airstrike on a hospital in southern Gaza overnight killed at least six people, the Health Ministry in the Palestinian enclave said Thursday.

events.title: Ukraine faces new Starshield disruptions as Trump envoys meet with Putin
events.summary: Hours after an American delegation touched down in Moscow for peace talks, Ukraine’s President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said his country’s military had experienced a renewed wave of “significant disruptions” to the Starshield satellite internet service, hampering its ability to defend itself against Russia.

events.title: Megaspeed, chip firm at center of Nvidia scandal, pledges to cooperate with U.S. investigation
events.summary: HONG KONG — Megaspeed, the tech company at the center of the Chinese spy scandal that engulfed Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, said Thursday it will cooperate with the U.S. government’s investigations into the matter.

events.title: U.S. charges 3 men with plotting multiple terror attacks, including on British air base
events.summary: One of the men helped direct the planned attack against the air base while he was in a U.S. prison, according to a Justice Department indictment.

events.title: Senior U.S. Army soldier arrested in U.K. on suspicion of assisting Russian intelligence
events.summary: The 41-year-old man was arrested “as part of an investigation by Counter Terrorism Policing” near the ⁠city of Gloucester, ​in the west ⁠of England, British police said.

events.title: U.S. moves military aircraft from British base amid Iran threats
events.summary: A U.S. official confirmed to NBC News that several military aircraft had left RAF Mildenhall as the security posture there had increased.

events.title: Nvidia opens investigation after CEO’s affair with alleged Chinese spy
events.summary: Huang acknowledged being unfaithful to his wife in an employee memo. The board said it has no reason to believe national security or company secrets were compromised.

events.title: Russell Brand sentenced to more than 10 years in prison for rape and sexual assaults
events.summary: The 51-year-old comedian and actor was found guilty in a British court last week.

events.title: Gunman with far-right views who killed 6 in Poland shooting rampage dies in hospital
events.summary: The man, described as being his mid-20s, was shot by police during Saturday’s attack in the main square of Poland’s second-largest city.

events.title: Parents, sister of far-right Kraków shooter found dead in family home
events.summary: Three bodies found in the home of the 24-year-old shooter in Saturday’s rampage in the heart of Kraków, Poland, belonged to the gunman’s family, police said.

events.title: Gunman kills 6 in ‘terror attack’ in Poland, officials say; 3 others found dead in his home
events.summary: A gunman described as having “ultranationalistic” beliefs fatally shot six people while driving through a public square Saturday in Krakow, Poland, officials said, in what the country’s defense minister characterized as a “terror attack.” Three of his relatives were later found dead in his home.

events.title: Pope Leo, who had cancer surgery weeks ago, begins South American tour
events.summary: Less than a month after Pope Leo XIV underwent cancer surgery, he set off on what the Vatican called a “homecoming” tour of South America.

events.title: Investors try to regain their footing after tech stocks tank
events.summary: Tech stocks in the U.S. steadied Friday after suffering one of their worst routs in years, as investors weighed the prospect of an AI investment slowdown.

events.title: Wave of bomb threats against European airliners triggers diversions and tarmac searches
events.summary: No explosives have been found, and it isn’t clear who or what is behind the calls, but the threats alone have caused chaos in the skies and airports.
